hook.text: The same drug at the same dose works for you but poisons your neighbor. Your genes decide how you metabolize medicine.

buildup.text: CYP enzymes in your liver break down most drugs. Variants in CYP genes make you a fast or slow metabolizer.

discovery.text: Slow metabolizers accumulate codeine dangerously. Ultra-fast ones convert it to morphine too quickly.

twist.text: Warfarin, a common blood thinner, needs genetic dosing. Wrong dose causes fatal bleeds.

climax.text: Pharmacogenomics means prescribing by genotype, not guesswork. The vision: the right drug, right dose, first time.

punchline.text: Your genes decide if a drug heals or harms.
